findings.summary: Benchmark N = 1024 figures: over eight seeds tolO falls 11-22% (D = 64) and 20-38.5% (D = 128), not 16-25% and 34-49%; causal rows gain least, and several ranges are narrower than the seed spread
findings.detail: 'Where Post does not tell o from 0', benchmark bullet: 'tolO is now 0.35 to 0.44 at D = 64 and 0.54 to 0.77 at D = 128, causal and not (...; on the same heads it falls by 16% to 25% and by 34% to 49%)'. I evaluated Model.lean's new tolO and the old recursion (tolOW at W = 0 with errB) on eight benchmark-like heads, seeds 41, 42 and 50-55, 128 evenly spread rows each (work/tol.out, tol_spread.out). The ratio new/old of the medians is 0.78-0.82 on non-causal rows and 0.86-0.89 on causal rows at D = 64, so the fall is 18-22% and 11-14%. At D = 128 it is 0.62-0.70 and 0.74-0.80, a fall of 30-38.5% and 20-26%. The causal rows fall below the stated ranges, and so does part of D = 128's non-causal. The new medians spread wider than the main table's ranges. D = 64: 0.41-0.43 against the table's 0.43-0.44, causal 0.34-0.38 against 0.35-0.38. D = 128: 0.65-0.84 against 0.70-0.77, causal 0.50-0.64 against 0.54-0.58. 0 meets Post: D = 64, 30-36% against 35-39% (causal 23-30% against 26-29%); D = 128, 49-59% against 52-56% (causal 38-50% against 42-45%). To resolve: give the falls separately for causal and non-causal rows, or as about 10-22% and 20-38%, and widen the N = 1024 ranges, or say they come from few heads. No conclusion changes: the tightening holds on every head I ran. The N = 2^14, v = 1, vEff = 0, one-key and test figures agree with mine.
findings.evidence: work/tol.py (python3 -I tol.py; tol.py spread; tol.py big), work/tol.out, tol_spread.out, tol_big.out.

notes: Re-review of the re-proof on DotE5m2ChunkLoss, gate 3d7848ee51b5e6a6. (1) assumption:dot cites DotE5m2ChunkLoss, the library's fact for fp8 x fp8 into float32 at 2^30, any precision. num.md lists it in the reviewer checklist's fp8 row and in the facts table, and its Lean is as num.md states. (2) spec. tolO's new parts (lS8, lC8, lP8, gD, coefD, accStep, errStep, stepC, stC, tolOW, blkV, blkAbsV) are explicit real expressions of the row's exact data and of X and Z, and they print as kernel, TVA or Mathlib names (work/print_spec.lean, print_spec.out); the axioms are unchanged. stepC's choice is a function of the row's data alone: per block and column it compares errStep/W + accStep on the two arms, with W = wsum*Fp(D, N, X, Z). tolO = min(tolOW(W), tolOW(0)), and tolOW(0) is term for term the round-24 recursion: gD cS8 = gA, coefD cC8 = coefS, and the chunk arm's accStep and errStep are accNext and errNext. scoreErr's errM is at most errB (errM_le_errB), so tolO is never above the old claim's at any admissible Z. Numerically, new/old is at most 1 on every element I evaluated. (3) Figures. These agree with mine: the test's data (non-causal unchanged on every element; causal about 1.5% lower; 0 meets Post at most 1 point fewer); scoreErr, pE and tolM unchanged on the host's data (the loss arm never wins in a score chunk beyond rounding); one key 0.29 |attnRef|; v = 1: 0.46, 0.70, 1.31, 2.43, 3.55, 5.46, 9.88; vEff = 0 at the cap 7.7e-6, 9.4e-6, 5.4e-5, with tolV still 7.63e-6, so those heads stay at ±0; the benchmark at N = 2^14 (20.1 -> 1.65 and 75 -> 3.71 non-causal, 3.5 -> 0.97 and 13.5 -> 1.94 causal, 0 rejected on 22% and 12% of causal elements); loss-arm blocks 47-62%; 4-8.5 times the floor. The benchmark N = 1024 exceptions are in the DOC finding.
